# sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          # gh-1692 AC3: the depth-1 clone pulls tip blobs from origin over
          # the runner's flaky link — the 10-16 submit leg died on "2876
          # bytes of body are still expected" (exit 128) with NO retry and
          # cost a whole TestFlight day. Bounded retry; a failed attempt
          # leaves a partial dir at $CLONE_TARGET which git refuses to
          # clone into, so it is removed before the next attempt.
          CLONE_RETRIES=3
          for attempt in $(seq 1 "$CLONE_RETRIES"); do
            if git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
              https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"; then
              break
            fi
            echo "git clone attempt ${attempt}/${CLONE_RETRIES} failed" >&2
            if [ "$attempt" -eq "$CLONE_RETRIES" ]; then
              echo "::error::git clone from origin failed after ${CLONE_RETRIES} attempts (gh-1692 AC3)" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
            sleep 10
          done
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with
      # cache: true on this PERSISTENT runner cost 5m39s setup (untar ~1GB
      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of
      # 19.7 min around a 4-min build (run 34815041052). The composite
      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,
      # exactly one download per pin bump, no cache POST step at all.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install — the runner's hardcoded
      # $HOME/.local/flutter is a stale 3.44.4, below the repo floor
      # >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260).
      - name: Setup Flutter (self-hosted)
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'

## Description

### Bug

No TestFlight build has shipped since 2026-10-13 (5 daily-publish runs red). Investigation across the 5 failing runs shows FOUR distinct failure signatures, the last one current and untracked:

| Date | Runner | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| 10-14 | Linux box | routing bug, exit 127 (`bundle: command not found`) — #1600 L1, fixed by #1663 (merged 10-18 08:38) |
| 10-15 | gh-sandbox-agents-Mac-mini | wrong Mac (no signing env) — same routing class |
| 10-16 | fa-m5-1 | **IPA built OK**; submit leg died on transient git mirror fetch (`2876 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) |
| 10-17, 10-18 | fa-m5-2 | `** ARCHIVE FAILED **` in fastlane `build_app`, ~6s after clean, with xcpretty printing NO error line (runs 39006178578, 39100442363) |

### Current root cause (10-17/10-18): fa-m5-2 archive environment

- `flutter build ios --release` succeeds (158MB Runner.app); the xcodebuild archive invocation dies within seconds — the classic signature of a signing/keychain/profile problem on that machine (provisioning profiles "Fa Profile"/"FaLiveActivity Profile", manual signing, teamID YP9HC3USZ3). The full error lives in `~/Library/Logs/gym/Runner-Runner.log` ON fa-m5-2 — invisible from GitHub.
- The merged routing fix #1663 uses `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` — this matches BOTH fa-m5-1 (proven good 10-16) AND fa-m5-2 (failing), and possibly the sandbox Mac-mini if it advertises those labels. Tomorrow's run is a coin flip. #1600 AC1 wanted the jobs pinned to the known-good runner (`fa-m5-1`).

### Fix

1. **Pin iOS build+submit jobs to fa-m5-1** (runner-name label) until fa-m5-2's signing environment is verified — or fix fa-m5-2 (install/refresh the distribution cert + both provisioning profiles; verify with a manual `xcodebuild archive` on that box).

3. **Never-again (transient)**: the mirror-fetch in the submit leg needs a bounded retry (10-16 exit 128 was a pure network hiccup and cost a whole day of TestFlight).
4. Routing regression guard (#1600 AC1's workflow-lint) should assert iOS jobs resolve to the intended runner LABEL SET, not merely "a macOS ARM64 machine".

### Acceptance criteria

1. Next daily-publish ships a TestFlight build (iOS legs on the pinned/verified runner).
2. An archive failure surfaces the real xcodebuild error in the GH log or a failure artifact — no more silent `ARCHIVE FAILED`.
3. Mirror-fetch retry in the submit leg.

### Evidence

- Runs: 38516656653 (10-14), 38686834918 (10-15), 38855794448 (10-16, build green on fa-m5-1 + submit exit 128), 39006178578 + 39100442363 (10-17/18, fa-m5-2 ARCHIVE FAILED).

# sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          # gh-1692 AC3: the depth-1 clone pulls tip blobs from origin over
          # the runner's flaky link — the 10-16 submit leg died on "2876
          # bytes of body are still expected" (exit 128) with NO retry and
          # cost a whole TestFlight day. Bounded retry; a failed attempt
          # leaves a partial dir at $CLONE_TARGET which git refuses to
          # clone into, so it is removed before the next attempt.
          CLONE_RETRIES=3
          for attempt in $(seq 1 "$CLONE_RETRIES"); do
            if git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
              https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"; then
              break
            fi
            echo "git clone attempt ${attempt}/${CLONE_RETRIES} failed" >&2
            if [ "$attempt" -eq "$CLONE_RETRIES" ]; then
              echo "::error::git clone from origin failed after ${CLONE_RETRIES} attempts (gh-1692 AC3)" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
            sleep 10
          done
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

def store_pubspec_version
  derived = ENV["BUILD_NAME"].to_s.strip
  return derived unless derived.empty?
  pubspec_path = File.expand_path("../pubspec.yaml", __dir__)
  return "1.0.0" unless File.exist?(pubspec_path)
  match = File.read(pubspec_path).match(/version:\s+([0-9.]+)/)

# lane failure the newest gym log tail is dumped into the job log so the
# failure is diagnosable from the GH run page without the artifact.
def print_gym_log_tail(lines: 80)
  log_dir = File.expand_path("~/Library/Logs/gym")
  return unless Dir.exist?(log_dir)

  newest = Dir.glob(File.join(log_dir, "**", "*.log")).max_by { |f| File.mtime(f) }
  return if newest.nil?

  UI.error("gh-1692: newest gym log tail (#{newest}) — the REAL xcodebuild error:")

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1694

- **Title**: gh-1692 [daily-publish] TestFlight dry 5 days: 4 chained failures — current: fa-m5-2 archive fails silently (xcpretty swallows xcodebuild error), routing still unpinned
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1692` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +387
- **Deletions**: -55
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T14:25:14Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T08:59:27Z

## PR Description

Closes #1692
## What changed

Un-breaks the 5-day TestFlight dry spell (gh-1692): pins the iOS build+submit jobs to the known-good runner by name, makes the next archive failure diagnosable from the GitHub run page, and bounds the remaining single-shot git transfer in the iOS chain.

## Key decisions

- `build-ios`/`submit-ios` now run on `[self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1]` — `macos-m5` alone was a coin flip between fa-m5-1 (good 10-16) and fa-m5-2 (silent `** ARCHIVE FAILED **`, unverified signing env). Runner-name label resolves to fa-m5-1 until fa-m5-2 is fixed.
- iOS `build_app` pins `xcodebuild_formatter: "xcbeautify"` (xcpretty swallowed the archive error); the lane prints the newest `~/Library/Logs/gym/*.log` tail into the job log on failure, and a `failure()`-gated step uploads the full gym logs as the `ios-gym-logs` artifact. A brew install step guarantees the formatter binary exists.
- The depth-1 mirror clone (last single-shot origin transfer in the iOS chain — the 10-16 exit-128 killer) now retries 3× with partial-dir cleanup between attempts, in both checkout steps; the mirror update itself keeps its gh-164 bounded-retry updater.
- Routing regression guard extended: `workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` AC1 now asserts the exact runner LABEL SET (incl. the `fa-m5-1` runner-name label) for the iOS legs; new `workflow_ios_archive_observability_test.dart` pins the xcbeautify/artifact/retry shape.

## How to verify

```bash
dart test test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart test/workflow_ios_archive_observability_test.dart
```

<details>
<summary>Change map</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  DP[daily-publish testflight leg] --> BM[build-mobile.yml]
  BM -->|runs-on: self-hosted + macos-m5 + fa-m5-1| BI[build-ios]
  BI -->|xcbeautify + gym-log tail + failure artifact| IPA[fa.ipa]
  BM -->|same pin + clone retry ×3| SI[submit-ios]
```

</details>

Note: the full `dart test` run passed 6693 tests with all failures confined to `test/integration/` + `test/browser_ext/` e2e suites that need a live LLM/PTY/browser backend (absent on this runner; pre-existing environmental). The run ended in a Dart VM native abort (`malloc_consolidate`, exit 134) after the last unit tests — also environmental, no Dart source was touched by this change.

# gh-1692: [daily-publish] TestFlight dry 5 days: 4 chained failures — current: fa-m5-2 archive fails silently (xcpretty swallows xcodebuild error), routing still unpinned

## Description

### Bug

No TestFlight build has shipped since 2026-10-13 (5 daily-publish runs red). Investigation across the 5 failing runs shows FOUR distinct failure signatures, the last one current and untracked:

| Date | Runner | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| 10-14 | Linux box | routing bug, exit 127 (`bundle: command not found`) — #1600 L1, fixed by #1663 (merged 10-18 08:38) |
| 10-15 | gh-sandbox-agents-Mac-mini | wrong Mac (no signing env) — same routing class |
| 10-16 | fa-m5-1 | **IPA built OK**; submit leg died on transient git mirror fetch (`2876 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) |
| 10-17, 10-18 | fa-m5-2 | `** ARCHIVE FAILED **` in fastlane `build_app`, ~6s after clean, with xcpretty printing NO error line (runs 39006178578, 39100442363) |

### Current root cause (10-17/10-18): fa-m5-2 archive environment

- `flutter build ios --release` succeeds (158MB Runner.app); the xcodebuild archive invocation dies within seconds — the classic signature of a signing/keychain/profile problem on that machine (provisioning profiles "Fa Profile"/"FaLiveActivity Profile", manual signing, teamID YP9HC3USZ3). The full error lives in `~/Library/Logs/gym/Runner-Runner.log` ON fa-m5-2 — invisible from GitHub.
- The merged routing fix #1663 uses `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` — this matches BOTH fa-m5-1 (proven good 10-16) AND fa-m5-2 (failing), and possibly the sandbox Mac-mini if it advertises those labels. Tomorrow's run is a coin flip. #1600 AC1 wanted the jobs pinned to the known-good runner (`fa-m5-1`).

### Fix

1. **Pin iOS build+submit jobs to fa-m5-1** (runner-name label) until fa-m5-2's signing environment is verified — or fix fa-m5-2 (install/refresh the distribution cert + both provisioning profiles; verify with a manual `xcodebuild archive` on that box).
2. **Never-again (observability)**: fastlane itself warns xcpretty "can result in missing some build errors" — switch the formatter to `xcbeautify` AND on failure upload `~/Library/Logs/gym/*.log` as a job artifact, so the next archive failure is diagnosable from the GH run page without shell access to the runner.
3. **Never-again (transient)**: the mirror-fetch in the submit leg needs a bounded retry (10-16 exit 128 was a pure network hiccup and cost a whole day of TestFlight).
4. Routing regression guard (#1600 AC1's workflow-lint) should assert iOS jobs resolve to the intended runner LABEL SET, not merely "a macOS ARM64 machine".

### Acceptance criteria

1. Next daily-publish ships a TestFlight build (iOS legs on the pinned/verified runner).
2. An archive failure surfaces the real xcodebuild error in the GH log or a failure artifact — no more silent `ARCHIVE FAILED`.
3. Mirror-fetch retry in the submit leg.

### Evidence

- Runs: 38516656653 (10-14), 38686834918 (10-15), 38855794448 (10-16, build green on fa-m5-1 + submit exit 128), 39006178578 + 39100442363 (10-17/18, fa-m5-2 ARCHIVE FAILED).
- Related: #1600 (closed via #1663 today), #1262 (CLI leg size budget — separate red leg blocking publish).

# from the latest tag + 1) wins — the committed pubspec carries the static
# 0.0.0-dev placeholder now, so the pubspec parse is only the LAST-resort
# fallback (a hand-run lane outside the CI env).
def store_pubspec_version
  derived = ENV["BUILD_NAME"].to_s.strip
  return derived unless derived.empty?
  pubspec_path = File.expand_path("../pubspec.yaml", __dir__)
  return "1.0.0" unless File.exist?(pubspec_path)
  match = File.read(pubspec_path).match(/version:\s+([0-9.]+)/)
  match ? match[1] : "1.0.0"
end

# gh-1692: xcpretty "can result in missing some build errors" (fastlane's
# own warning) — the 10-17/10-18 daily runs printed `** ARCHIVE FAILED **`
# with NO error line and the real xcodebuild error only lived in
# ~/Library/Logs/gym/ on the runner. xcbeautify keeps error lines, and on
# lane failure the newest gym log tail is dumped into the job log so the
# failure is diagnosable from the GH run page without the artifact.
def print_gym_log_tail(lines: 80)
  log_dir = File.expand_path("~/Library/Logs/gym")
  return unless Dir.exist?(log_dir)

  newest = Dir.glob(File.join(log_dir, "**", "*.log")).max_by { |f| File.mtime(f) }
  return if newest.nil?

  UI.error("gh-1692: newest gym log tail (#{newest}) — the REAL xcodebuild error:")
  File.readlines(newest).last(lines).each { |l| UI.error(l.chomp) }
end

- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +387
- **Deletions**: -55
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T14:25:14Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T08:59:27Z

## PR Description

Closes #1692
## What changed

Un-breaks the 5-day TestFlight dry spell (gh-1692): pins the iOS build+submit jobs to the known-good runner by name, makes the next archive failure diagnosable from the GitHub run page, and bounds the remaining single-shot git transfer in the iOS chain.

## Key decisions

- `build-ios`/`submit-ios` now run on `[self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1]` — `macos-m5` alone was a coin flip between fa-m5-1 (good 10-16) and fa-m5-2 (silent `** ARCHIVE FAILED **`, unverified signing env). Runner-name label resolves to fa-m5-1 until fa-m5-2 is fixed.
- iOS `build_app` pins `xcodebuild_formatter: "xcbeautify"` (xcpretty swallowed the archive error); the lane prints the newest `~/Library/Logs/gym/*.log` tail into the job log on failure, and a `failure()`-gated step uploads the full gym logs as the `ios-gym-logs` artifact. A brew install step guarantees the formatter binary exists.
- The depth-1 mirror clone (last single-shot origin transfer in the iOS chain — the 10-16 exit-128 killer) now retries 3× with partial-dir cleanup between attempts, in both checkout steps; the mirror update itself keeps its gh-164 bounded-retry updater.
- Routing regression guard extended: `workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` AC1 now asserts the exact runner LABEL SET (incl. the `fa-m5-1` runner-name label) for the iOS legs; new `workflow_ios_archive_observability_test.dart` pins the xcbeautify/artifact/retry shape.

## How to verify

```bash
dart test test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart test/workflow_ios_archive_observability_test.dart
```

<details>
<summary>Change map</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  DP[daily-publish testflight leg] --> BM[build-mobile.yml]
  BM -->|runs-on: self-hosted + macos-m5 + fa-m5-1| BI[build-ios]
  BI -->|xcbeautify + gym-log tail + failure artifact| IPA[fa.ipa]
  BM -->|same pin + clone retry ×3| SI[submit-ios]
```

</details>

Note: the full `dart test` run passed 6693 tests with all failures confined to `test/integration/` + `test/browser_ext/` e2e suites that need a live LLM/PTY/browser backend (absent on this runner; pre-existing environmental). The run ended in a Dart VM native abort (`malloc_consolidate`, exit 134) after the last unit tests — also environmental, no Dart source was touched by this change.

=====
# gh-1692: [daily-publish] TestFlight dry 5 days: 4 chained failures — current: fa-m5-2 archive fails silently (xcpretty swallows xcodebuild error), routing still unpinned

## Description

### Bug

No TestFlight build has shipped since 2026-10-13 (5 daily-publish runs red). Investigation across the 5 failing runs shows FOUR distinct failure signatures, the last one current and untracked:

| Date | Runner | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| 10-14 | Linux box | routing bug, exit 127 (`bundle: command not found`) — #1600 L1, fixed by #1663 (merged 10-18 08:38) |
| 10-15 | gh-sandbox-agents-Mac-mini | wrong Mac (no signing env) — same routing class |
| 10-16 | fa-m5-1 | **IPA built OK**; submit leg died on transient git mirror fetch (`2876 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) |
| 10-17, 10-18 | fa-m5-2 | `** ARCHIVE FAILED **` in fastlane `build_app`, ~6s after clean, with xcpretty printing NO error line (runs 39006178578, 39100442363) |

### Current root cause (10-17/10-18): fa-m5-2 archive environment

- `flutter build ios --release` succeeds (158MB Runner.app); the xcodebuild archive invocation dies within seconds — the classic signature of a signing/keychain/profile problem on that machine (provisioning profiles "Fa Profile"/"FaLiveActivity Profile", manual signing, teamID YP9HC3USZ3). The full error lives in `~/Library/Logs/gym/Runner-Runner.log` ON fa-m5-2 — invisible from GitHub.
- The merged routing fix #1663 uses `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` — this matches BOTH fa-m5-1 (proven good 10-16) AND fa-m5-2 (failing), and possibly the sandbox Mac-mini if it advertises those labels. Tomorrow's run is a coin flip. #1600 AC1 wanted the jobs pinned to the known-good runner (`fa-m5-1`).

### Fix

1. **Pin iOS build+submit jobs to fa-m5-1** (runner-name label) until fa-m5-2's signing environment is verified — or fix fa-m5-2 (install/refresh the distribution cert + both provisioning profiles; verify with a manual `xcodebuild archive` on that box).
2. **Never-again (observability)**: fastlane itself warns xcpretty "can result in missing some build errors" — switch the formatter to `xcbeautify` AND on failure upload `~/Library/Logs/gym/*.log` as a job artifact, so the next archive failure is diagnosable from the GH run page without shell access to the runner.
3. **Never-again (transient)**: the mirror-fetch in the submit leg needs a bounded retry (10-16 exit 128 was a pure network hiccup and cost a whole day of TestFlight).
4. Routing regression guard (#1600 AC1's workflow-lint) should assert iOS jobs resolve to the intended runner LABEL SET, not merely "a macOS ARM64 machine".

### Acceptance criteria

1. Next daily-publish ships a TestFlight build (iOS legs on the pinned/verified runner).
2. An archive failure surfaces the real xcodebuild error in the GH log or a failure artifact — no more silent `ARCHIVE FAILED`.
3. Mirror-fetch retry in the submit leg.

### Evidence

- Runs: 38516656653 (10-14), 38686834918 (10-15), 38855794448 (10-16, build green on fa-m5-1 + submit exit 128), 39006178578 + 39100442363 (10-17/18, fa-m5-2 ARCHIVE FAILED).
- Related: #1600 (closed via #1663 today), #1262 (CLI leg size budget — separate red leg blocking publish).

# sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          # gh-1692 AC3: the depth-1 clone pulls tip blobs from origin over
          # the runner's flaky link — the 10-16 submit leg died on "2876
          # bytes of body are still expected" (exit 128) with NO retry and
          # cost a whole TestFlight day. Bounded retry; a failed attempt
          # leaves a partial dir at $CLONE_TARGET which git refuses to
          # clone into, so it is removed before the next attempt.
          CLONE_RETRIES=3
          for attempt in $(seq 1 "$CLONE_RETRIES"); do
            if git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
              https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"; then
              break
            fi
            echo "git clone attempt ${attempt}/${CLONE_RETRIES} failed" >&2
            if [ "$attempt" -eq "$CLONE_RETRIES" ]; then
              echo "::error::git clone from origin failed after ${CLONE_RETRIES} attempts (gh-1692 AC3)" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
            sleep 10
          done
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with

      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,

# from the latest tag + 1) wins — the committed pubspec carries the static
# 0.0.0-dev placeholder now, so the pubspec parse is only the LAST-resort
# fallback (a hand-run lane outside the CI env).
def store_pubspec_version
  derived = ENV["BUILD_NAME"].to_s.strip
  return derived unless derived.empty?
  pubspec_path = File.expand_path("../pubspec.yaml", __dir__)
  return "1.0.0" unless File.exist?(pubspec_path)
  match = File.read(pubspec_path).match(/version:\s+([0-9.]+)/)
  match ? match[1] : "1.0.0"
end

# gh-1692: xcpretty "can result in missing some build errors" (fastlane's
# own warning) — the 10-17/10-18 daily runs printed `** ARCHIVE FAILED **`
# with NO error line and the real xcodebuild error only lived in
# ~/Library/Logs/gym/ on the runner. xcbeautify keeps error lines, and on
# lane failure the newest gym log tail is dumped into the job log so the
# failure is diagnosable from the GH run page without the artifact.
def print_gym_log_tail(lines: 80)
  log_dir = File.expand_path("~/Library/Logs/gym")
  return unless Dir.exist?(log_dir)

  newest = Dir.glob(File.join(log_dir, "**", "*.log")).max_by { |f| File.mtime(f) }
  return if newest.nil?

  UI.error("gh-1692: newest gym log tail (#{newest}) — the REAL xcodebuild error:")
  File.readlines(newest).last(lines).each { |l| UI.error(l.chomp) }
end

  value = ENV[name].to_s.strip
  UI.user_error!("#{name} is not set — #{what}") if value.empty?
  value
end

Tomorrow's run is a coin flip. #1600 AC1 wanted the jobs pinned to the known-good runner (`fa-m5-1`).

1. **Pin iOS build+submit jobs to fa-m5-1** (runner-name label) until fa-m5-2's signing environment is verified — or fix fa-m5-2 (install/refresh the distribution cert + both provisioning profiles; verify with a manual `xcodebuild archive` on that box).

3. **Never-again (transient)**: the mirror-fetch in the submit leg needs a bounded retry (10-16 exit 128 was a pure network hiccup and cost a whole day of TestFlight).
4. Routing regression guard (#1600 AC1's workflow-lint) should assert iOS jobs resolve to the intended runner LABEL SET, not merely "a macOS ARM64 machine".

### Acceptance criteria

1. Next daily-publish ships a TestFlight build (iOS legs on the pinned/verified runner).
2. An archive failure surfaces the real xcodebuild error in the GH log or a failure artifact — no more silent `ARCHIVE FAILED`.
3. Mirror-fetch retry in the submit leg.

- Runs: 38516656653 (10-14), 38686834918 (10-15), 38855794448 (10-16, build green on fa-m5-1 + submit exit 128), 39006178578 + 39100442363 (10-17/18, fa-m5-2 ARCHIVE FAILED).

# sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          # gh-1692 AC3: the depth-1 clone pulls tip blobs from origin over
          # the runner's flaky link — the 10-16 submit leg died on "2876
          # bytes of body are still expected" (exit 128) with NO retry and
          # cost a whole TestFlight day. Bounded retry; a failed attempt
          # leaves a partial dir at $CLONE_TARGET which git refuses to
          # clone into, so it is removed before the next attempt.
          CLONE_RETRIES=3
          for attempt in $(seq 1 "$CLONE_RETRIES"); do
            if git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
              https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"; then
              break
            fi
            echo "git clone attempt ${attempt}/${CLONE_RETRIES} failed" >&2
            if [ "$attempt" -eq "$CLONE_RETRIES" ]; then
              echo "::error::git clone from origin failed after ${CLONE_RETRIES} attempts (gh-1692 AC3)" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
            sleep 10
          done
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at

# from the latest tag + 1) wins — the committed pubspec carries the static
# 0.0.0-dev placeholder now, so the pubspec parse is only the LAST-resort
# fallback (a hand-run lane outside the CI env).
def store_pubspec_version
  derived = ENV["BUILD_NAME"].to_s.strip
  return derived unless derived.empty?
  pubspec_path = File.expand_path("../pubspec.yaml", __dir__)
  return "1.0.0" unless File.exist?(pubspec_path)
  match = File.read(pubspec_path).match(/version:\s+([0-9.]+)/)
  match ? match[1] : "1.0.0"
end

# gh-1692: xcpretty "can result in missing some build errors" (fastlane's
# own warning) — the 10-17/10-18 daily runs printed `** ARCHIVE FAILED **`
# with NO error line and the real xcodebuild error only lived in
# ~/Library/Logs/gym/ on the runner. xcbeautify keeps error lines, and on
# lane failure the newest gym log tail is dumped into the job log so the
# failure is diagnosable from the GH run page without the artifact.
def print_gym_log_tail(lines: 80)
  log_dir = File.expand_path("~/Library/Logs/gym")
  return unless Dir.exist?(log_dir)

  newest = Dir.glob(File.join(log_dir, "**", "*.log")).max_by { |f| File.mtime(f) }
  return if newest.nil?

  UI.error("gh-1692: newest gym log tail (#{newest}) — the REAL xcodebuild error:")
  File.readlines(newest).last(lines).each { |l| UI.error(l.chomp) }
end

  value = ENV[name].to_s.strip
  UI.user_error!("#{name} is not set — #{what}") if value.empty?
  value
end

# gh-1692: [daily-publish] TestFlight dry 5 days: 4 chained failures — current: fa-m5-2 archive fails silently (xcpretty swallows xcodebuild error), routing still unpinned

## Description

### Bug

No TestFlight build has shipped since 2026-10-13 (5 daily-publish runs red). Investigation across the 5 failing runs shows FOUR distinct failure signatures, the last one current and untracked:

| Date | Runner | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| 10-14 | Linux box | routing bug, exit 127 (`bundle: command not found`) — #1600 L1, fixed by #1663 (merged 10-18 08:38) |
| 10-15 | gh-sandbox-agents-Mac-mini | wrong Mac (no signing env) — same routing class |
| 10-16 | fa-m5-1 | **IPA built OK**; submit leg died on transient git mirror fetch (`2876 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) |
| 10-17, 10-18 | fa-m5-2 | `** ARCHIVE FAILED **` in fastlane `build_app`, ~6s after clean, with xcpretty printing NO error line (runs 39006178578, 39100442363) |

### Current root cause (10-17/10-18): fa-m5-2 archive environment

- `flutter build ios --release` succeeds (158MB Runner.app); the xcodebuild archive invocation dies within seconds — the classic signature of a signing/keychain/profile problem on that machine (provisioning profiles "Fa Profile"/"FaLiveActivity Profile", manual signing, teamID YP9HC3USZ3). The full error lives in `~/Library/Logs/gym/Runner-Runner.log` ON fa-m5-2 — invisible from GitHub.
- The merged routing fix #1663 uses `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` — this matches BOTH fa-m5-1 (proven good 10-16) AND fa-m5-2 (failing), and possibly the sandbox Mac-mini if it advertises those labels. Tomorrow's run is a coin flip. #1600 AC1 wanted the jobs pinned to the known-good runner (`fa-m5-1`).

### Fix

1. **Pin iOS build+submit jobs to fa-m5-1** (runner-name label) until fa-m5-2's signing environment is verified — or fix fa-m5-2 (install/refresh the distribution cert + both provisioning profiles; verify with a manual `xcodebuild archive` on that box).
2. **Never-again (observability)**: fastlane itself warns xcpretty "can result in missing some build errors" — switch the formatter to `xcbeautify` AND on failure upload `~/Library/Logs/gym/*.log` as a job artifact, so the next archive failure is diagnosable from the GH run page without shell access to the runner.
3. **Never-again (transient)**: the mirror-fetch in the submit leg needs a bounded retry (10-16 exit 128 was a pure network hiccup and cost a whole day of TestFlight).
4. Routing regression guard (#1600 AC1's workflow-lint) should assert iOS jobs resolve to the intended runner LABEL SET, not merely "a macOS ARM64 machine".

### Acceptance criteria

1. Next daily-publish ships a TestFlight build (iOS legs on the pinned/verified runner).
2. An archive failure surfaces the real xcodebuild error in the GH log or a failure artifact — no more silent `ARCHIVE FAILED`.
3. Mirror-fetch retry in the submit leg.

+// last two runs failed with `** ARCHIVE FAILED **` in fastlane's
+// build_app while xcpretty printed NO error line — the real xcodebuild
+// error only lived in ~/Library/Logs/gym/ ON the runner, invisible from
+// GitHub. The 10-16 run died earlier on a transient single-shot git
+// mirror fetch (exit 128, "2876 bytes of body are still expected") and
+// cost a whole day of TestFlight.
+//
+// Static workflow-shape asserts (the "workflow-shape test never-again"
+// pattern of workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart):
+//
+//   AC2  the archive failure is diagnosable from the GH run page: the
+//        iOS lane pins xcbeautify as the xcodebuild formatter (xcpretty
+//        swallows build errors — fastlane's own warning), the workflow
+//        installs xcbeautify on the self-hosted runner, and on failure
+//        ~/Library/Logs/gym/*.log is uploaded as a job artifact.
+//   AC3  the git fetch/clone legs of the iOS chain carry a BOUNDED
+//        retry — no single-shot origin transfer may red the leg.
+import 'dart:io';
+
+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+import 'package:yaml/yaml.dart';
+
+String read(String path) => File(path).readAsStringSync();
+
+YamlMap jobsOf(String workflowPath) =>
+    loadYaml(read(workflowPath))['jobs'] as YamlMap;
+
+List<YamlMap> stepsOf(String workflowPath, String job) =>
+    ((jobsOf(workflowPath)[job] as YamlMap)['steps'] as YamlList)
+        .whereType<YamlMap>()
+        .toList();
+
+void main() {
+  const mobile = '.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml';
+
+  group('AC2 — archive failure is diagnosable from the GH run page', () {
+    test('Fastfile build_app pins xcbeautify, never xcpretty (gh-1692)', () {
+      final fastfile = read('flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile');
+      final buildApp = fastfile.indexOf('build_app(');
+      expect(buildApp, greaterThan(-1), reason: 'build_app must exist');
+      final options = fastfile.substring(
+        buildApp,
+        fastfile.indexOf("\n    end", buildApp),
+      );
+      expect(
+        options,
+        contains('xcodebuild_formatter: "xcbeautify"'),
+        reason:
+            'xcpretty "can result in missing some build errors" (fastlane '
+            'own warning) — the 10-17/10-18 runs printed `** ARCHIVE '
+            'FAILED **` with NO error line. xcbeautify keeps error lines '
+            'in the GH log (gh-1692).',
+      );
+      expect(
+        options.contains('xcpretty'),
+        isFalse,
+        reason:
+            'the xcpretty formatter must be gone from the iOS build_app '
+            'options (gh-1692)',
+      );
+      // The lane must also dump the newest gym log tail into the GH log
+      // on failure, so the real xcodebuild error is readable WITHOUT
+      // downloading the artifact.
+      expect(
+        fastfile,
+        contains('print_gym_log_tail'),
+        reason:
+            'on lane failure the newest ~/Library/Logs/gym/*.log tail '
+            'must be printed into the job log — the next archive failure '
+            'must surface the real xcodebuild error in the GH log '
+            '(gh-1692 AC2)',
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('build-ios installs xcbeautify before the archive step', () {
+      final steps = stepsOf(mobile, 'build-ios');

+      final buildIdx = steps.indexWhere(

+          reason: 'build-ios must install xcbeautify (gh-1692)');
+      expect(buildIdx, greaterThan(-1));
+      expect(
+        installIdx,
+        lessThan(buildIdx),
+        reason:
+            'xcbeautify must be installed BEFORE the archive — a missing '
+            'formatter binary must never silently re-introduce the '
+            'xcpretty class (gh-1692)',
+      );
+    });
+

+      final steps = stepsOf(mobile, 'build-ios');
+      final upload = steps.where(

+            (s['uses']?.toString() ?? '').contains('upload-artifact') &&
+            (s['if']?.toString() ?? '') == 'failure()' &&
+            (s['with'] as YamlMap?)?['path']

+      );
+      expect(

+        hasLength(1),
+        reason:
+            'exactly one failure-gated artifact upload of '
+            '~/Library/Logs/gym/ — the gym log holds the REAL xcodebuild '

_Previous review discussions for PR #1694._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` line 1053

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-19):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: pin `if-no-files-found: error` on the gym-log artifact upload**

AC2's promise is that the *next* archive failure is diagnosable from GitHub. This step is the full-fidelity half of that promise, but it inherits the `upload-artifact` default `if-no-files-found: warn` — if the glob matches nothing (e.g. the lane failed before gym created its log, `HOME` differs from the lane's, or a future formatter change moves the log location), the step prints a warning and **succeeds with no artifact**, and the only signal left is the 80-line tail in the job log. On this persistent runner the log dir also accumulates across runs, so "some file matched" and "this run's log matched" are not the same bar.

Given this repo's never-again test style, I'd also expect the companion test to pin the input (it currently asserts only the `path`/`if`/`uses` shape).

```yaml
        with:
          name: ios-gym-logs
          path: ~/Library/Logs/gym/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14
```

(Tilde expansion in `path` is fine — `actions/upload-artifact` README, "Environment Variables and Tilde Expansion" explicitly supports `~`.)

---

### Thread 2 — `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` line 86

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-19):
💡 **SUGGESTION: substring `contains` doesn't enforce the "exact LABEL SET" the test name claims**

`runsOn` is the YAML-serialized `runs-on` value and `contains(label)` is plain substring matching, so the guard passes for `fa-m5-1b`, `not-fa-m5-1`, or an *extra* label like `fa-m5-2` riding alongside. The PR description and test title say the AC1 assert is the exact runner label set — parsing the list and comparing sets would make it true:

```dart
final runsOn = (jobs[id] as YamlMap)['runs-on'];
final labels = runsOn is YamlList
    ? runsOn.map((e) => e.toString()).toSet()
    : {runsOn.toString()};
expect(labels, jobEntry.value.toSet());
```

Cheap to do now while the map shape is already in this diff.

---

### Thread 3 — `flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile` line 82

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-19):
💡 **SUGGESTION: newest-by-mtime can dump a *previous* run's gym log on this persistent runner**

If `build_app` fails before gym creates its log for this run (e.g. early xcodebuild invocation error or formatter spawn failure), `max_by { File.mtime }` picks up the log of the *previous* daily run and `UI.error`s 80 lines of a stale, unrelated failure into the job log — a new flavor of misleading output in exactly the observability path gh-1692 is hardening. The printed filename mitigates this (a reader can spot the old timestamp), but consider guarding on mtime age, e.g. skip (or annotate) when the newest log is older than the lane start:

```ruby
newest = Dir.glob(File.join(log_dir, "**", "*.log")).max_by { |f| File.mtime(f) }
return if newest.nil? || File.mtime(newest) < (lane_start - 60)
```

Also note the workflow artifact (all of `~/Library/Logs/gym/`) intentionally keeps full history, so nothing is lost by narrowing the tail.

---

### Thread 4 — `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` line 732

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-19):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the retry loop is guarded only by string-shape asserts — consider an executable selftest**

The new AC3 tests assert the *text* of this loop (`CLONE_RETRIES=3`, `for attempt in`, `::error::`), which pins today's shape but can't catch a bash-logic regression inside the loop (e.g. a future edit breaking the `rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"` ordering the test reasons about). The repo already has the pattern for this: `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (+ `aab-gate-selftest.yml`) exercises the mirror updater's retry script for real. The same harness could simulate a failing-then-succeeding `git clone` (a stub `git` on `PATH` that fails N times) and assert the loop exits 0 after exactly N attempts and hard-fails after 3. Precedent exists, so this is optional — the static pins are still a big improvement over no guard.

---

blocks.text:
# sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          # gh-1692 AC3: the depth-1 clone pulls tip blobs from origin over
          # the runner's flaky link — the 10-16 submit leg died on "2876
          # bytes of body are still expected" (exit 128) with NO retry and
          # cost a whole TestFlight day. Bounded retry; a failed attempt
          # leaves a partial dir at $CLONE_TARGET which git refuses to
          # clone into, so it is removed before the next attempt.
          CLONE_RETRIES=3
          for attempt in $(seq 1 "$CLONE_RETRIES"); do
            if git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
              https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"; then
              break
            fi
            echo "git clone attempt ${attempt}/${CLONE_RETRIES} failed" >&2
            if [ "$attempt" -eq "$CLONE_RETRIES" ]; then
              echo "::error::git clone from origin failed after ${CLONE_RETRIES} attempts (gh-1692 AC3)" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
            sleep 10
          done
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with
      # cache: true on this PERSISTENT runner cost 5m39s setup (untar ~1GB
      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of
      # 19.7 min around a 4-min build (run 34815041052). The composite
      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,
      # exactly one download per pin bump, no cache POST step at all.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install — the runner's hardcoded
      # $HOME/.local/flutter is a stale 3.44.4, below the repo floor
      # >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260).
      - name: Setup Flutter (self-hosted)
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'

      - name: Setup environment (self-hosted)
        run: |
          echo "/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          echo "/opt/homebrew/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      # gh-1692 AC2: the iOS lane pins xcbeautify as the xcodebuild
      # formatter (xcpretty "can result in missing some build errors" —
      # the 10-17/10-18 archive failures printed NO error line). Homebrew
      # keeps it a one-time install on this persistent runner; the step
      # verifies the binary so a missing formatter can never silently
      # re-introduce the xcpretty class.
      - name: Install xcbeautify (xcodebuild formatter, gh-1692)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if command -v xcbeautify >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "xcbeautify already installed: $(xcbeautify --version)"
          else
            brew install xcbeautify
          fi
          xcbeautify --version

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # gh-798 AC1/AC2: fail FAST before any build minute is spent when the
      # version about to be stamped is not above ASC's approved floor
      # (#785's class: altool 90062 at the END of the build). Reads the
      # SAME version source the build lane stamps (BUILD_NAME of the
      # version job); the lane skips named without ASC secrets (the upload
      # leg skips too) and fails closed if ASC is unreachable (E1, one
      # retry). The AC4 marker line lands in the leg log either way.
      - name: Assert TestFlight version floor
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:

# from the latest tag + 1) wins — the committed pubspec carries the static
# 0.0.0-dev placeholder now, so the pubspec parse is only the LAST-resort
# fallback (a hand-run lane outside the CI env).
def store_pubspec_version
  derived = ENV["BUILD_NAME"].to_s.strip
  return derived unless derived.empty?
  pubspec_path = File.expand_path("../pubspec.yaml", __dir__)
  return "1.0.0" unless File.exist?(pubspec_path)
  match = File.read(pubspec_path).match(/version:\s+([0-9.]+)/)
  match ? match[1] : "1.0.0"
end

# gh-1692: xcpretty "can result in missing some build errors" (fastlane's
# own warning) — the 10-17/10-18 daily runs printed `** ARCHIVE FAILED **`
# with NO error line and the real xcodebuild error only lived in
# ~/Library/Logs/gym/ on the runner. xcbeautify keeps error lines, and on
# lane failure the newest gym log tail is dumped into the job log so the
# failure is diagnosable from the GH run page without the artifact.
def print_gym_log_tail(lines: 80)
  log_dir = File.expand_path("~/Library/Logs/gym")
  return unless Dir.exist?(log_dir)

  newest = Dir.glob(File.join(log_dir, "**", "*.log")).max_by { |f| File.mtime(f) }
  return if newest.nil?

  UI.error("gh-1692: newest gym log tail (#{newest}) — the REAL xcodebuild error:")
  File.readlines(newest).last(lines).each { |l| UI.error(l.chomp) }
end

def require_env!(name, what)
  value = ENV[name].to_s.strip
  UI.user_error!("#{name} is not set — #{what}") if value.empty?
  value
end

            if git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \

            if [ "$attempt" -eq "$CLONE_RETRIES" ]; then

# gh-1692: [daily-publish] TestFlight dry 5 days: 4 chained failures — current: fa-m5-2 archive fails silently (xcpretty swallows xcodebuild error), routing still unpinned

## Description

### Bug

No TestFlight build has shipped since 2026-10-13 (5 daily-publish runs red). Investigation across the 5 failing runs shows FOUR distinct failure signatures, the last one current and untracked:

| Date | Runner | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| 10-14 | Linux box | routing bug, exit 127 (`bundle: command not found`) — #1600 L1, fixed by #1663 (merged 10-18 08:38) |
| 10-15 | gh-sandbox-agents-Mac-mini | wrong Mac (no signing env) — same routing class |
| 10-16 | fa-m5-1 | **IPA built OK**; submit leg died on transient git mirror fetch (`2876 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) |
| 10-17, 10-18 | fa-m5-2 | `** ARCHIVE FAILED **` in fastlane `build_app`, ~6s after clean, with xcpretty printing NO error line (runs 39006178578, 39100442363) |

### Current root cause (10-17/10-18): fa-m5-2 archive environment

- `flutter build ios --release` succeeds (158MB Runner.app); the xcodebuild archive invocation dies within seconds — the classic signature of a signing/keychain/profile problem on that machine (provisioning profiles "Fa Profile"/"FaLiveActivity Profile", manual signing, teamID YP9HC3USZ3). The full error lives in `~/Library/Logs/gym/Runner-Runner.log` ON fa-m5-2 — invisible from GitHub.
- The merged routing fix #1663 uses `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` — this matches BOTH fa-m5-1 (proven good 10-16) AND fa-m5-2 (failing), and possibly the sandbox Mac-mini if it advertises those labels. Tomorrow's run is a coin flip. #1600 AC1 wanted the jobs pinned to the known-good runner (`fa-m5-1`).

### Fix

1. **Pin iOS build+submit jobs to fa-m5-1** (runner-name label) until fa-m5-2's signing environment is verified — or fix fa-m5-2 (install/refresh the distribution cert + both provisioning profiles; verify with a manual `xcodebuild archive` on that box).
2. **Never-again (observability)**: fastlane itself warns xcpretty "can result in missing some build errors" — switch the formatter to `xcbeautify` AND on failure upload `~/Library/Logs/gym/*.log` as a job artifact, so the next archive failure is diagnosable from the GH run page without shell access to the runner.
3. **Never-again (transient)**: the mirror-fetch in the submit leg needs a bounded retry (10-16 exit 128 was a pure network hiccup and cost a whole day of TestFlight).
4. Routing regression guard (#1600 AC1's workflow-lint) should assert iOS jobs resolve to the intended runner LABEL SET, not merely "a macOS ARM64 machine".

### Acceptance criteria

1. Next daily-publish ships a TestFlight build (iOS legs on the pinned/verified runner).
2. An archive failure surfaces the real xcodebuild error in the GH log or a failure artifact — no more silent `ARCHIVE FAILED`.
3. Mirror-fetch retry in the submit leg.

### Evidence

- Runs: 38516656653 (10-14), 38686834918 (10-15), 38855794448 (10-16, build green on fa-m5-1 + submit exit 128), 39006178578 + 39100442363 (10-17/18, fa-m5-2 ARCHIVE FAILED).

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-19):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: pin `if-no-files-found: error` on the gym-log artifact upload**

AC2's promise is that the *next* archive failure is diagnosable from GitHub. This step is the full-fidelity half of that promise, but it inherits the `upload-artifact` default `if-no-files-found: warn` — if the glob matches nothing (e.g. the lane failed before gym created its log, `HOME` differs from the lane's, or a future formatter change moves the log location), the step prints a warning and **succeeds with no artifact**, and the only signal left is the 80-line tail in the job log. On this persistent runner the log dir also accumulates across runs, so "some file matched" and "this run's log matched" are not the same bar.

Given this repo's never-again test style, I'd also expect the companion test to pin the input (it currently asserts only the `path`/`if`/`uses` shape).

```yaml
        with:
          name: ios-gym-logs
          path: ~/Library/Logs/gym/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14
```

(Tilde expansion in `path` is fine — `actions/upload-artifact` README, "Environment Variables and Tilde Expansion" explicitly supports `~`.)

# sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          # gh-1692 AC3: the depth-1 clone pulls tip blobs from origin over
          # the runner's flaky link — the 10-16 submit leg died on "2876
          # bytes of body are still expected" (exit 128) with NO retry and
          # cost a whole TestFlight day. Bounded retry; a failed attempt
          # leaves a partial dir at $CLONE_TARGET which git refuses to
          # clone into, so it is removed before the next attempt.
          CLONE_RETRIES=3
          for attempt in $(seq 1 "$CLONE_RETRIES"); do
            if git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
              https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"; then
              break
            fi
            echo "git clone attempt ${attempt}/${CLONE_RETRIES} failed" >&2
            if [ "$attempt" -eq "$CLONE_RETRIES" ]; then
              echo "::error::git clone from origin failed after ${CLONE_RETRIES} attempts (gh-1692 AC3)" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
            sleep 10
          done
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with

      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of
      # 19.7 min around a 4-min build (run 34815041052). The composite
      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,
      # exactly one download per pin bump, no cache POST step at all.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install — the runner's hardcoded

      # >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260).

        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'

      # gh-1692 AC2: the iOS lane pins xcbeautify as the xcodebuild

# from the latest tag + 1) wins — the committed pubspec carries the static
# 0.0.0-dev placeholder now, so the pubspec parse is only the LAST-resort
# fallback (a hand-run lane outside the CI env).
def store_pubspec_version
  derived = ENV["BUILD_NAME"].to_s.strip
  return derived unless derived.empty?
  pubspec_path = File.expand_path("../pubspec.yaml", __dir__)
  return "1.0.0" unless File.exist?(pubspec_path)
  match = File.read(pubspec_path).match(/version:\s+([0-9.]+)/)
  match ? match[1] : "1.0.0"
end

# gh-1692: xcpretty "can result in missing some build errors" (fastlane's
# own warning) — the 10-17/10-18 daily runs printed `** ARCHIVE FAILED **`
# with NO error line and the real xcodebuild error only lived in
# ~/Library/Logs/gym/ on the runner. xcbeautify keeps error lines, and on
# lane failure the newest gym log tail is dumped into the job log so the
# failure is diagnosable from the GH run page without the artifact.
def print_gym_log_tail(lines: 80)
  log_dir = File.expand_path("~/Library/Logs/gym")
  return unless Dir.exist?(log_dir)

  newest = Dir.glob(File.join(log_dir, "**", "*.log")).max_by { |f| File.mtime(f) }
  return if newest.nil?

  UI.error("gh-1692: newest gym log tail (#{newest}) — the REAL xcodebuild error:")
  File.readlines(newest).last(lines).each { |l| UI.error(l.chomp) }
end

  value = ENV[name].to_s.strip
  UI.user_error!("#{name} is not set — #{what}") if value.empty?
  value
end

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: pin `if-no-files-found: error` on the gym-log artifact upload**

This step is the full-fidelity half of AC2's promise (the *next* archive failure must be diagnosable from the GitHub run page), but it inherits `actions/upload-artifact`'s default `if-no-files-found: warn` — if the glob matches nothing (lane failed before gym created its log, `HOME` differs between the runner daemon and the lane, a future formatter change moves the log location), the step warns and **succeeds with no artifact**. The only signal left would then be the 80-line tail in the job log. On this persistent runner the log dir also accumulates across runs, so "some file matched" and "this run's log matched" are not the same bar.

The companion test (`workflow_ios_archive_observability_test.dart`) asserts only the `path`/`if`/`uses` shape — in this repo's never-again test style it should pin the input too.

```yaml
        with:
          name: ios-gym-logs
          path: ~/Library/Logs/gym/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14
```

(Tilde expansion in `path` is fine — `actions/upload-artifact` README, "Environment Variables and Tilde Expansion" explicitly supports `~`.)

Re-raised from the previous review round: the rework pushes on this PR were merge-only and did not address this thread.

💡 **SUGGESTION: substring `contains` doesn't enforce the "exact LABEL SET" the test name claims**

`runsOn` is the YAML-serialized `runs-on` value and `contains(label)` is plain substring matching, so the guard passes for `fa-m5-1b`, `not-fa-m5-1`, or an *extra* label like `fa-m5-2` riding alongside — the exact coin flip gh-1692 exists to eliminate. The PR description and test title say AC1 asserts the exact runner label set; parsing the list and comparing sets would make that true:

```dart
final runsOn = (jobs[id] as YamlMap)['runs-on'];
final labels = runsOn is YamlList
    ? runsOn.map((e) => e.toString()).toSet()
    : {runsOn.toString()};
expect(labels, jobEntry.value.toSet());
```

Cheap to do now while the map shape is already in this diff.

Re-raised from the previous review round: the rework pushes on this PR were merge-only and did not address this thread.

💡 **SUGGESTION: newest-by-mtime can dump a *previous* run's gym log on this persistent runner**

If `build_app` fails before gym creates its log for this run (early xcodebuild invocation error, formatter spawn failure), `max_by { File.mtime }` picks up the *previous* daily run's log and `UI.error`s 80 lines of a stale, unrelated failure into the job log — a new flavor of misleading output in exactly the observability path gh-1692 is hardening. The printed filename mitigates this (a reader can spot the old timestamp), but consider guarding on mtime age, e.g. skip (or annotate) when the newest log predates the lane start:

```ruby
newest = Dir.glob(File.join(log_dir, "**", "*.log")).max_by { |f| File.mtime(f) }
return if newest.nil? || File.mtime(newest) < (lane_start - 60)
```

The workflow artifact (all of `~/Library/Logs/gym/`) intentionally keeps full history, so nothing is lost by narrowing the tail.

Re-raised from the previous review round: the rework pushes on this PR were merge-only and did not address this thread.

💡 **SUGGESTION: the retry loop is guarded only by string-shape asserts — consider an executable selftest**

The new AC3 tests assert the *text* of this loop (`CLONE_RETRIES=3`, `for attempt in`, `::error::`), which pins today's shape but can't catch a bash-logic regression inside the loop (e.g. a future edit breaking the `rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"` ordering the test reasons about). The repo already has the pattern: `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (+ `aab-gate-selftest.yml`) exercises the mirror updater's retry script for real. The same harness could simulate a failing-then-succeeding `git clone` (a stub `git` on `PATH` that fails N times) and assert the loop exits 0 after exactly N attempts and hard-fails after 3. Precedent exists, so this is optional — the static pins are still a big improvement over no guard, and I verified the loop's control flow by hand (clone failure is inside the `if` guard so `set -e` can't abort it; exhaustion hits the explicit `exit 1`).

Re-raised from the previous review round: the rework pushes on this PR were merge-only and did not address this thread.

💡 **SUGGESTION: the clone-retry block is duplicated verbatim across `build-ios` and `submit-ios`**

The ~19-line retry loop (comment + `CLONE_RETRIES` + `for attempt in … sleep 10` + `::error::` exhaustion) is copy-pasted into both checkout steps (build-ios ~L732, submit-ios ~L1301). The repo already factors shared checkout bash into scripts — `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` is the shared entry point for the mirror update, guarded once by `update_git_mirror_selftest.sh`. Extracting `scripts/clone_with_retry.sh` would give the two legs one source of truth, make the executable-selftest idea (comment4) cover both legs at once, and shrink the inline YAML. Optional — the duplication is contained to one file and the string-shape tests pin both copies.

### Acceptance criteria

1. Next daily-publish ships a TestFlight build (iOS legs on the pinned/verified runner).

# PR Discussion History

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` line 1053

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-19):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: pin `if-no-files-found: error` on the gym-log artifact upload**

AC2's promise is that the *next* archive failure is diagnosable from GitHub. This step is the full-fidelity half of that promise, but it inherits the `upload-artifact` default `if-no-files-found: warn` — if the glob matches nothing (e.g. the lane failed before gym created its log, `HOME` differs from the lane's, or a future formatter change moves the log location), the step prints a warning and **succeeds with no artifact**, and the only signal left is the 80-line tail in the job log. On this persistent runner the log dir also accumulates across runs, so "some file matched" and "this run's log matched" are not the same bar.

Given this repo's never-again test style, I'd also expect the companion test to pin the input (it currently asserts only the `path`/`if`/`uses` shape).

```yaml
        with:
          name: ios-gym-logs
          path: ~/Library/Logs/gym/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14
```

(Tilde expansion in `path` is fine — `actions/upload-artifact` README, "Environment Variables and Tilde Expansion" explicitly supports `~`.)

---

### Thread 2 — `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` line 86

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-19):
💡 **SUGGESTION: substring `contains` doesn't enforce the "exact LABEL SET" the test name claims**

`runsOn` is the YAML-serialized `runs-on` value and `contains(label)` is plain substring matching, so the guard passes for `fa-m5-1b`, `not-fa-m5-1`, or an *extra* label like `fa-m5-2` riding alongside. The PR description and test title say the AC1 assert is the exact runner label set — parsing the list and comparing sets would make it true:

```dart

final labels = runsOn is YamlList
```

If `build_app` fails before gym creates its log for this run (e.g. early xcodebuild invocation error or formatter spawn failure), `max_by { File.mtime }` picks up the log of the *previous* daily run and `UI.error`s 80 lines of a stale, unrelated failure into the job log — a new flavor of misleading output in exactly the observability path gh-1692 is hardening. The printed filename mitigates this (a reader can spot the old timestamp), but consider guarding on mtime age, e.g. skip (or annotate) when the newest log is older than the lane start:

```ruby
newest = Dir.glob(File.join(log_dir, "**", "*.log")).max_by { |f| File.mtime(f) }
return if newest.nil? || File.mtime(newest) < (lane_start - 60)
```

Also note the workflow artifact (all of `~/Library/Logs/gym/`) intentionally keeps full history, so nothing is lost by narrowing the tail.

### Thread 4 — `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` line 732

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-19):

The new AC3 tests assert the *text* of this loop (`CLONE_RETRIES=3`, `for attempt in`, `::error::`), which pins today's shape but can't catch a bash-logic regression inside the loop (e.g. a future edit breaking the `rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"` ordering the test reasons about). The repo already has the pattern for this: `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (+ `aab-gate-selftest.yml`) exercises the mirror updater's retry script for real. The same harness could simulate a failing-then-succeeding `git clone` (a stub `git` on `PATH` that fails N times) and assert the loop exits 0 after exactly N attempts and hard-fails after 3. Precedent exists, so this is optional — the static pins are still a big improvement over no guard.

# sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          # gh-1692 AC3: the depth-1 clone pulls tip blobs from origin over
          # the runner's flaky link — the 10-16 submit leg died on "2876
          # bytes of body are still expected" (exit 128) with NO retry and
          # cost a whole TestFlight day. Bounded retry; a failed attempt
          # leaves a partial dir at $CLONE_TARGET which git refuses to
          # clone into, so it is removed before the next attempt.
          CLONE_RETRIES=3
          for attempt in $(seq 1 "$CLONE_RETRIES"); do
            if git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
              https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"; then
              break
            fi
            echo "git clone attempt ${attempt}/${CLONE_RETRIES} failed" >&2
            if [ "$attempt" -eq "$CLONE_RETRIES" ]; then
              echo "::error::git clone from origin failed after ${CLONE_RETRIES} attempts (gh-1692 AC3)" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
            sleep 10
          done
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with

      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of

      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,
